newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Mir suddenly postpones planned docking.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Mir suddenly postpones planned docking.

text.p: The Mir space station abruptly postponed a planned docking with its cargo resupply ship on Sunday after a technical malfunction, a NASA official said.
"They were giving some preliminary commands to see if it (the Progress cargo ship) was controllable," said the official. "Maybe the computer got confused with the different commands."
The redocking with the seven-metre (23 feet) long Progress had been scheduled to take place at 5.54 p.m. Moscow time (1354 GMT).
"It was put off for at least one day," the NASA official said just an hour and a half before the redocking had been due to go ahead.

The manoeuvre was to repeat a procedure carried out on June 25 when a different Progress vehicle docking with Mir collided into the station's Spektr module, causing a major loss of power in the worst accident of the space station's 11-year history.
On Sunday however, the Mir crew of two Russians and one British-American had planned to attempt the docking in automatic rather than manual pilot as in June.
